title: The system: a social network's home timeline, built on write and merged on read
caption: One post is written once, then fanned out asynchronously to follower timelines and to notifications; the feed service merges in the few accounts too big to push.

steps.text: The author posts. The post API writes it once to the post store, by id and onto the author's own recent-posts list.
It publishes a PostCreated event to a log partitioned by author and returns. The author waits about 20 ms, not for the fan-out.
Fan-out workers consume the event, page through the author's followers 1 000 at a time and add the post id to each follower's timeline (capped at the newest 800 ids).
Notifications are a second, independent consumer of the same event: only the followers who turned alerts on get a push.
A reader opens the app. The feed service reads their timeline ids and the short list of very big accounts they follow, one cache read.
It pulls the recent posts of those big accounts from the post store, merges everything by time and hydrates the bodies in one multi-get.

scenarios.name: Celebrity posts
scenarios.summary: An account with 30 M followers posts. Pushing would be 30 M writes; the hybrid writes once and lets readers pull it.

steps.text: The post is written once, exactly like any other.
The event carries the author's follower count. The workers see it is above the threshold (say 500 k) and skip the timeline writes.
The notifier still runs, but only for opted-in followers, spread over a few minutes so the push provider is not flooded.
Each reader who follows the account gets the post merged in at read time from the author's recent list.

scenarios.name: Fan-out worker crash
scenarios.summary: A worker dies half-way through a big follower list. The event is not lost and the retry does no harm.

steps.text: A worker crashes after writing to 400 k of 900 k followers. It never committed its log offset.
The log redelivers the event to another worker, which resumes from the last follower page it checkpointed.
Timeline entries are keyed by post id, so any page written twice is a no-op. Followers late in the list just see the post a few seconds later.
Readers were never blocked: the feed kept serving whatever each timeline held.

scenarios.name: Threshold change
scenarios.summary: Operators lower the celebrity threshold from 1 M to 500 k followers to cut fan-out cost: a config change, not a migration.

steps.text: The new threshold is published as config; workers and the feed service pick it up within seconds.
Accounts between 500 k and 1 M stop being pushed: their next posts are written once and skipped by the workers.
Their followers' lists of big accounts are refreshed, so the feed starts pulling those authors.
Older pushed posts from those authors are still in the timelines; the merge drops duplicates by post id until they age out.
